subject: Reserved throughput & GPU sizing — action items from discovery
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>

Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved throughput & GPU sizing — action items from discovery

Hi Stuart — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment before the sizing validation run: 

Summary of FinLytics targets (from the call)
- P95 end-to-end latency (non-streaming completions) for typical customer queries (avg 100-150 tokens): <= 150 ms
- Streaming: initial response < 50 ms; token cadence <= 60 ms/token for steady stream
- Expected steady-state concurrency: 20 concurrent active streams
- Peak concurrency (burst): 60 concurrent streams for short windows (1-3 minutes)
- Expected average response length: ~90 tokens; target sustained throughput: 400 requests/min (approx. 36k tokens/min)
- SLA: 99.5% availability for the reserved capacity pool, with automatic fallback to hosted tier for overflow

What we propose for validation
1) Reserve a Dedicated pool with the following profiles to test:
   - GPU A: A10G (cost-optimized)
   - GPU B: A100 40GB (balanced perf)
   - GPU C: H100 (max throughput / headroom)
2) Run a 4-hour stress validation per GPU variant: start at 50% of projected load, ramp to 120% over 75 minutes, hold for 60 minutes, sharp burst for 3 minutes to exercise ingress autoscaling.
3) Workloads: 80% streaming flows, 20% non-streaming completions; mix of 64/128/512 token tails as discussed.
4) Metrics to capture: P50/P95/P99 latency, token-per-second throughput, GPU utilization, memory headroom, queue times, tail latencies during warm-up, and KV cache hit ratios.
5) Failure modes: simulate cold-cache, KV cache warm start, and ephemeral network jitter.

Attachments: I attached the perf matrix we sketched during the call and our internal GPU benchmark summary.
[attachment: finlytics_perf_matrix_v1.xlsx (sheet: target-slo, 85KB)]
[attachment: gpu-variant-benchmarks.pdf (6 pages, 420KB)]

Immediate asks for FinLytics (short):
- Can you confirm the engineering contact who will own the test window and provide a token for smoke tests? (we need an API key / service account for the dedicated preview)
- Any blackout windows for Sept 21–24 when you'd prefer we avoid heavy ingress?

Proposed timeline
- Confirm test owners & credentials by EOD Thu (2026-09-17)
- Schedule validation slot the week of Sept 28 (we'll allocate 4 hours per GPU variant)

I’ll loop in Ben (ops lead) and Karthik (SRE) to finalize the test harness and reporting template. If this looks good, we’ll send a formal mutual action plan + HubSpot update.

Thanks — Hannah

Ben / Karthik / Vanessa — forwarding Stuart's confirmation. Two quick asks so we can scope the validation harness: 

Ben: can your team prepare a parametric driver that supports the ramp profile (50% -> 120% -> hold -> 3-min burst) and mixes streaming/non-streaming as per Hannah's note? Include the ability to toggle quantization path (fp16 vs int8) and to simulate cold KV-cache starts. Also capture per-request timing (client-to-first-byte and per-token cadence).

Karthik: plan the canary policies and the observability hooks. We need traces that tie request id -> GPU instance -> kernel selection. Add a quick script to pull GPU occupancy and per-process GPU memory every 30s and upload to the shared Drive folder.

Vanessa: pricing impact — post-validation, we'll produce a recommended reserved capacity SKU per GPU variant with expected unit cost / token. Please put a template in the Drive so we can fill it after the run.

Target to have drivers and dashboards ready for smoke runs by Sept 24. Ben/Karthik please confirm ETA by EOD Wed.

Thanks, H

-----Original Message-----
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Reserved throughput & GPU sizing — action items from discovery

All — we can deliver the driver and basic dashboards. Plan: 
- Driver: Golang harness that can simulate both HTTP streaming connections and batched completion requests; paramizable QPS, concurrent streams, token-length distribution, and quantization toggle.
- Observability: Prometheus + Grafana dashboard template; additional script for GPU traces (nvidia-smi snapshots + perf counters where available).
- Test infra: spin up isolated dedicated pools (A10G / A100 / H100) in our staging region (us-west-2). We'll attach the FinLytics service account for auth.

ETA: drivers + dashboards ready for smoke by Thu 2026-09-24 18:00 PDT. We should be able to run the 4-hour long tests the week of Sept 28 — Sept 30 morning US ET looks feasible for the heavy-burst windows Stuart requested.

Notes on expected outcomes and tradeoffs (preliminary)
- A10G: cost-effective, will likely meet steady-state for 64-128 token responses at 20 concurrent streams, but may show higher P99 tail during 3-min bursts and for 512-token tails.
- A100-40GB: better headroom for sustained throughput and larger KV cache (gives better latency consistency for 512-token tails).
- H100: best throughput for mixed streaming + long-context scoring; will give us headroom to turn down reserved pool size or reduce autoscaling latency.

We will capture per-GPU recommendations in the Drive sheet (linked). If we see the A10G tail latencies break the 150 ms P95 during bursts, recommended path will be a mixed pool (A10G primary, A100 canary) with routing policy to failover to higher-tier GPUs for bursts.

Ben
